# Vicem — Diet the Context, Pass the Baton

> **Hit Claude Code's 5-hour quota mid-feature? Or watching Cursor / Codex slow to a crawl after 150k tokens of context rot?** > > **Vicem** compacts your active coding session by **80–92% net effective tokens** ([Measured Eval](./docs/BENCHMARK.md) — via deterministic AST code skeletonization with `[pure]` / `[effects: ...]` tags + SHA-256-checked, secret-redacted MCP rehydration) and hands off a hardened `.vicem/BATON.md` across **Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Antigravity IDE, and Web AI** in 3 seconds — with **`0` npm dependencies** and **`0` network calls**. > > ⭐ **Tip:** Click **Star** (top-right) to bookmark this repo for the next time your coding agent hits a 5-hour quota limit or context rot.


🎬 15s Relay Overview — Watch in 1080p60 with sound (MP4) · All Links & Quick Copy

--- ## ⚡ 10-Second Quick Start (`npx` — Zero Install) ### 1. Run the Local Handoff GUI or Pass a Baton Immediately ```bash # Launch the local Handoff GUI (3-step guided handoff, preview confirmation & manual recovery) npx -y vicem-cli gui # Or pack a compressed baton from your current repo & hand off in 1 command npx -y vicem-cli codex npx -y vicem-cli claude npx -y vicem-cli cursor # Or auto-configure global `vicem` CLI + MCP servers across all installed agents npx -y vicem-cli setup ``` ### 2. Add as an Agent Skill & MCP Server in 1 Line (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor) ```bash # Install the Agent Skill globally (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, Windsurf) npx skills add RAKKUNN/vicem -g # Claude Code MCP Server claude mcp add vicem -- npx -y vicem-cli mcp # OpenAI Codex CLI MCP Server codex mcp add vicem -- npx -y vicem-cli mcp ```
Cursor / Windsurf / Claude Desktop (mcp.json config) Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`, or `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "vicem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "vicem-cli", "mcp"] } } } ```

🌐 Try Zero-Install Browser Sandbox (GitHub Pages) · 📦 npm (vicem-cli / @rakkunn/vicem) · 📊 Cache Hit Rate & Break-Even Eval · 🔒 Security & Zero-Network Proof

--- ## Visual Overview

1. **Review your work (`01 · Source conversation`)**: Select the active project and source conversation, and inspect or edit the extracted handoff goal. 2. **Choose a destination (`02 · Choose a destination`)**: Pick the target agent (`Claude Code`, `OpenAI Codex`, `Cursor`, `Antigravity`, `Gemini CLI`, `Windsurf`, `VS Code`, `Web Chat`) and delivery action (`Open the app`, `Open in terminal`, or `Prepare handoff only`). 3. **Review and hand off (`03 · Review handoff`)**: Inspect the exact `.vicem/BATON.md` summary before anything is written or launched. If automatic launch is unavailable, copy the saved `BATON.md` path, shell continuation command, and start prompt directly from the recovery panel. ```text $ npx -y vicem-cli codex ╭─ VICEM CONTEXT BATON & DIET RECEIPT ──────────────────────────────────╮ │ Source Session : Claude Code (sess-9f3a2c · 42 turns harvested) │ │ Context Diet : 184,200 tok ($2.76) ──► 14,800 tok ($0.22) [-91.9%] │ │ Code Skeletons : 18 files compressed (31 bodies indexed in ledger) │ │ Security Guard : 2 secrets redacted (OPENAI_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY) │ │ Relay Target : OpenAI Codex CLI (interactive TTY handoff ready) │ ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ [OK] [Vicem] Baton written to .vicem/BATON.md (182ms). Launching codex... ``` --- ## How Side-Effect-Tagged AST Skeletonization + MCP Rehydration Works Instead of lossy LLM summarization that forgets exact type contracts or hides side effects, Vicem keeps all imports, types, and signatures intact inside `.vicem/BATON.md`, annotates every elided body with **deterministic AST purity & side-effect tags** (`[pure]` vs `[effects: fs-write, proc, net, state, fs-read, throws, async]` with 1-hop intra-file propagation), and indexes raw bodies in `.vicem/ledger.json`: ```ts // What the receiving agent sees in .vicem/BATON.md (disk file untouched): export interface JwtPayload { sub: string; exp: number; role: 'admin' | 'user'; } export function normalizeBearerHeader(rawHeader: string): string { /* ... [pure] */ } export async function verifySessionToken(rawToken: string, secret: string): Promise { /* ... [effects: fs-read, throws, async] */ } ``` When the receiving agent actually needs to edit `verifySessionToken`, it calls the MCP tool **`vicem_rehydrate("src/auth.ts", "verifySessionToken")`** (optionally with `include_callees: true`) for SHA-256-checked, secret-redacted AST rehydration on demand — while `.vicem/metrics.json` (`vicem stats`) tracks your live **Skeleton Cache Hit Rate (`CHR`)** and **Net Token Reduction (`NTR`)** ([see full benchmark & break-even curve](./docs/BENCHMARK.md)). | Pipeline Stage | Before Vicem (Raw Session) | After Vicem Baton & Diet (v1.3.0) | Measured Impact | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Session Handoff** | 40+ turns of raw JSONL / SQLite history locked in one tool | Extracts `Goal`, `Done`, `Failed Attempts`, `Immediate NEXT` & `git diff` into `.vicem/BATON.md` | **< 3s handoff** across 12+ CLI, IDE & Web AI agents | | **2. Side-Effect AST Skeletonizer** | Full source files with unchanged function bodies (`~59,100 tok`) | Signatures + `[pure]` / `[effects: ...]` tags + 1-hop call graph; bodies in `.vicem/ledger.json` | **90–98% cache hit rate**, **-84% to -92% net tokens** ([eval](./docs/BENCHMARK.md)) | | **3. Test & Log Slimmer** | Verbose ANSI spinners & `node_modules` stack frames (`~45,000 tok`) | Failing assertion + top 5 user-code stack frames (`~1,200 tok`) | **-95% log noise** | | **4. Data & Noise Gate** | Lockfiles, build bundles, and huge JSON / CSV / SQL dumps | Lockfiles dropped; data files reduced to inferred schema + 2 sample rows | **-98% data bloat** | | **5. 4-Pillar Safety & Injection Guard** | Plaintext `.env` keys, skeleton stub writes, or indirect prompt-injection in logs | Regex + Shannon-entropy secret scrubbing, `BatonInjectionGuard` (Unicode Trojan / fence-escape / hijack defanging) & `SkeletonWriteGuard` | **4-layer defense** & **`0` npm dependencies** | ### Architectural Benchmark vs. Existing Context Packers Measured on Apple M2 Pro (`darwin-arm64`, Node `v25.9.0`, `/usr/bin/time -l` median of 5 runs, OpenAI `o200k_base` BPE tokenizer) on a polyglot JS/TS/Python/JSON repository (`87,460` total tokens / `70,682` code-only tokens, containing an inline test secret and an untrusted prompt-injection comment): | Tool / Architecture Category | Install Footprint (Deps) | Median Time | Peak RSS | Output (`o200k_base`) | Reduction | Reversible Bodies (`rehydrate`) | Secret / Injection Defense | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Vicem v1.3.0 (`diet` — Task Baton + Hot-Expand)** | **0.47 MB (`0`)** | **133 ms** | **55 MB** | **1,051 tok** | **-98.8%** | **Yes (active fn inline, 0 RPC)** | **Redacted / Defanged** | | **Vicem v1.3.0 (`vicem map` — Whole-Repo Map)** | **0.47 MB (`0`)** | **161 ms** | **77 MB** | **8,678 tok** | **-90.1%** | **Yes (221 symbols via MCP)** | **Redacted / Defanged** | | **Vicem v1.3.0 (`--compact-all` Full Baton)** | **0.47 MB (`0`)** | **219 ms** | **77 MB** | **9,721 tok** | **-88.9%** | **Yes (221 symbols via MCP)** | **Redacted / Defanged** | | Tree-sitter WASM Repo Packer (`--compress`, Full) | ~102 MB (`84`) | 333 ms | 208 MB | 18,587 tok | -78.7% | No (one-way deletion) | Secrets only / Injection leaked | | Tree-sitter WASM Repo Packer (`--compress`, Code-Only) | ~102 MB (`84`) | 331 ms | 207 MB | 9,844 tok | -86.1%* | No (one-way deletion) | Secrets only / Injection leaked | | Standard XML Repo Packer (Default) | ~102 MB (`84`) | 274 ms | 164 MB | 79,934 tok | -8.6% | Full raw dump | Leaked / Leaked | | Python Repo Ingestor | ~25 MB | 419 ms | 145 MB | 79,650 tok | -8.9% | Full raw dump | Leaked / Leaked | | Raw File Concatenator | ~0.2 MB | 36 ms | 18 MB | 87,537 tok | 0% | Full raw dump | Leaked / Leaked | *Code-only comparison (`70,682` raw code tokens, excluding JSON fixtures): `vicem map` produces **8,583 tok (-87.9%)** in **160 ms** while keeping all 221 elided functions restorable on demand via `vicem_rehydrate`. See [`docs/BENCHMARK.md`](./docs/BENCHMARK.md) for the reproducible `CHR`/`NTR` evaluation and break-even curve. --- ## Direct CLI Commands & Offline Source Setup ```bash # 1. Launch the interactive Desktop Utility GUI vicem gui # 2. Compact current bloated session in-place (Context Rot Rescue) vicem self # 3. Pass baton to any CLI, IDE, or Web AI target vicem codex | vicem claude | vicem gemini | vicem cursor | vicem windsurf | vicem vscode | vicem web # 4. Return baton to previous agent & auto-unmount temporary rules vicem back # 5. Extract & smart-patch code blocks from a Web AI clipboard reply vicem land # 6. Build reversible whole-repo map, pin architectural decisions & install Claude lifecycle hooks vicem map vicem decide "Keep zero npm dependencies and preserve backward-compatible API" vicem init --agent-hooks # 7. Inspect Skeleton Cache Hit Rate (CHR), Net Token Savings (NTR) & run diagnostics vicem stats vicem doctor npm run bench ```
Offline / Air-Gapped Source Clone Installer (No npm required) ```bash git clone https://github.com/RAKKUNN/vicem.git && cd vicem ./vicem.mjs setup # or double-click setup.command (macOS/Linux) / setup.bat (Windows) ``` For browser-only air-gapped environments without Node.js, open **`index.html`** directly in Chrome, Edge, Brave, or Safari (enforced by `connect-src 'none'` CSP).
--- ## Supply-Chain Verification & Minimal TCB Verify zero third-party dependencies and cryptographic artifact integrity in one command: ```bash # 1. Confirm zero npm dependencies node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json')).dependencies ?? '0 dependencies')" # 2. Verify SHA-256 checksums of all core artifacts shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS # 3. Run the 775-test automated suite node --test test/*.test.mjs ``` ## Reviewed handoffs and safe recovery Start the local interface with `node vicem.mjs gui`. Select the project and source conversation, edit the goal, choose the destination and launch mode, then review before delivery. Technical telemetry is available under details. - `node vicem.mjs codex --preview`: preview without saving handoff artifacts or launching an app. - `node vicem.mjs codex --preview --json`: structured preview for automation. - `node vicem.mjs status --json` / `node vicem.mjs history --json`: inspect recorded outcomes. - `node vicem.mjs undo `: restore instruction changes for that handoff only. If those instructions have since changed, recovery refuses to overwrite them. This does not undo agent edits to source code. The GUI rejects a reviewed handoff if its content changes before delivery. Delivery and application launch do not establish that an agent has read the context: reception remains unconfirmed. The preview token is a consistency check, not authentication. Legacy `--dry-run` still writes handoff artifacts; use `--preview` for a read-only preview. Validation: automated unit/integration tests and local macOS browser checks. Windows/Linux real-agent launch and actual target-agent reception are not certified by these tests. GUI and CLI share preparation, rule mounting, outcome history and instruction recovery; platform launch adapters remain distinct. See [compatibility verification](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) for tested operating systems, actual agent read proofs, and limitations. ### Automatic launch and manual continuation Windows CLI/package behavior is verified in native CI on Node 22 and 24. Windows desktop integration remains Preview; desktop auto-launch on every OS is best effort. [View the passing CI run](https://github.com/RAKKUNN/vicem/actions/runs/41040234570) and [the precise support scope](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md). If automatic launch fails, the handoff stays saved. The GUI provides **Copy command**, **Copy start prompt**, and the saved file path. Open the destination manually, select your project, and paste the start prompt. CLI failures provide the same guide. Successful delivery does not confirm that an agent read it.

Start the local interface with node vicem.mjs gui. Select the project and source conversation, edit the goal, choose the destination and launch mode, then review before delivery. Technical telemetry is available under details.

The GUI rejects a reviewed handoff if its content changes before delivery. Delivery and application launch do not establish that an agent has read the context: reception remains unconfirmed.
